newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Gutnick plans A$75m gold search.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Gutnick plans A$75m gold search.

text.p: Australian mining entrepreneur Joseph Gutnick plans to spend A$75 million on gold exploration in 1997, all but a fraction of it in Australia.

The exploration budget, one of the largest among Australia's legion of mining companies and prospectors, targets the mineral rich goldfields of the state of Western Australia and underscores his strategy of growing his companies through discovery, Gutnick told Reuters.
"We will be spending most of the funds in Australia, which offers us great opportunities," he said.
In total, just under A$400 million was spent on gold exploration in Western Australia in 1995/96 (July/June), industry figures show.

The main asset of the Gutnick stable of resource companies, which span gold, nickel and diamonds, Great Central Mines Ltd, is mining the giant Bronzewing gold lode and the Jundee deposits, which are located in the Yandal Belt mineral prvince, a key target for further exploration.
In January, Great Central outlined a new mineral resource estimate at Jundee's Barton Deeps prospect of one million ounces of gold and a further 600,000 ounces at Bronzewing.
The revision took the total estimated resource at Jundee and Bronzewing to 6.35 million ounces of gold.
Turning to the gold price, Gutnick said the market was largely being dictated by influential investors outside the mining community.
"The hedge funds and speculators are affecting the gold price ... they've got to be watched," he said.
He said there was little a mining company could do other than to hedge a percentage of future mine production to reduce exposure to the vagaries of the international market.
"There are forces at play which we have no control over," Gutnick said.
About 66 percent of Great Central's gold production is hedged, he said.
Great Central's hedge book covers 1.728 million ounces at an average price of A$607 an ounce, compared with a current price of about A$460.
"I believe we're going to see more volatility in the gold price," he said.
Gutnick is attending the Australian Gold Conference here.
